title: Friendships That Simply Stop
sentences: Very few of my friendships have ever ended in anything resembling an argument.
Almost all of them ended by gradually running out of occasions to meet at all.
One person moves away, the shared routine disappears, and nothing ever replaces it.
There is rarely a single moment you could point to afterwards and clearly identify.
That absence of a moment is what makes the loss so unexpectedly difficult to discuss.
You cannot easily mourn something that neither party ever declared to be over.
I have started treating certain friendships as things that genuinely require maintenance.
It feels distinctly unromantic, and it has kept three of them alive so far.
The ones I lost were not weaker than the ones I have somehow managed to keep.
They were simply the ones where neither of us ever bothered to make arrangements.
